free_tier.stated: A grant of 'un montant maximum de 30 000 EUR sous condition', covering up to 50 percent of eligible expenses and up to 70 percent for some company categories, over a programme of at most 24 months, for a PME under the European SME definition.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The rule that no expense incurred before the application date is eligible makes this a forward-looking budget rather than a rebate, so it cannot pay for compute already burned while testing; it composes with a vendor trial only if the trial is structured as an expense after filing.

limits.value: The beneficiary must be an entity registered in France and less than one year old, or a physical person in pre-creation accompanied by a labelled incubator, so the door needs either French incorporation or a French support structure willing to sponsor the file.

evidence.proved: 'Aide sous forme de subvention d'un montant maximum de 30 000 EUR sous condition'; 'Cette aide peut couvrir jusqu'a 50 % des depenses eligibles et selon la categorie de l'entreprise, jusqu'a 70 %'; 'Programme d'une duree maximum de 24 mois', quoted
'Aucune depense engagee anterieurement a la date de depot de la demande d'aide ne peut etre retenue', quoted

'Entrepreneurs personnes physiques, y compris s'ils sont constitues en entreprise individuelle, sous reserve d'etre accompagnes par des structures ... dediees a l'accompagnement de projets innovants', and 'Montant maximum : 30 000 EUR', quoted, regional French Tech network
'50 000 euros : c'est le plafond de la Bourse French Tech', stated by a grant aggregator, which the Bpifrance page contradicts

notes: This finding contains a refutation. the aggregator figure is wrong or describes a different scheme, and the smaller number is recorded. The physical-person route is the only clause that admits somebody without a company, and it is conditioned on an incubator that has its own selection committee, which converts a formality into a discretionary review. Three readings were considered. (a) A foreign founder can apply through a French incubator partner: plausible, because the pre-creation route does not name a nationality and the eligibility criterion is French registration of the future company. (b) French residence is required: unverified, nothing read states it. (c) The grant can pay for cloud compute: plausible, since it funds 'depenses de R&D internes et externes', but no expense schedule was read. What would settle it: the Bpifrance notice de cahier des charges for the current year, which was not published on the page read.
